value.text:
Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them.

He has played 299 games and carried the ball 2,805 times for 20,416 yards, better than seven yards a carry, with 367 rushing touchdowns. He catches it too: 235 receptions for 1,871 yards and 60 more scores. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards say the league noticed.

It started in Tennessee, where he was Rookie of the Year on the Titans team that won it all in Y72. Seattle came next, then the Jets, where he won a second ring in Y77 and ran for 212 yards in a single game in Y78, a record that stood until Y85. Four seasons in Atlanta followed, and then the road led back to New York, where he finished his career after Y87.

Malakai Sawyer, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles.

K'Lavon Settle played 255 games for the 49ers from Y73 to Y87 and made 3,185 tackles, about twelve and a half every time he took the field. He intercepted 36 passes. He was never credited with a sack or a forced fumble, because his job was never to gamble. He read the play, closed the distance and brought the ball carrier down, snap after snap, season after season.

He did it without a ring and without an individual award. What he left instead is the deepest tackle total the league has seen.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. K'Lavon Settle, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
